quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: The past form of 'delegate' — to give part of your work or authority to someone else.
quests.explanation: Delegated means passed specific tasks or responsibilities to someone else. Good managers delegate rather than trying to do everything themselves.
quests.textToSpeak: The project manager delegated several tasks to junior members of the team.
quests.textWithBlanks: The project manager ___ several tasks to junior members of the team.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: A person applying for a job or competing for a position.
quests.explanation: A candidate is someone being considered for a job, award, or position. 'Panel interview' means several interviewers were assessing candidates together.
quests.textToSpeak: Only one candidate answered every question confidently during the panel interview.
quests.textWithBlanks: Only one ___ answered every question confidently during the panel interview.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Not connected to or useful for the matter being discussed.
quests.explanation: Irrelevant describes something unrelated to the topic at hand. Legal and academic writing often needs to filter out irrelevant details.
quests.textToSpeak: Most of the information in the report turned out to be irrelevant to the case.
quests.textWithBlanks: Most of the information in the report turned out to be ___ to the case.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Money awarded to a student to help pay for their education.
quests.explanation: A scholarship covers education costs, usually awarded based on merit or need. 'Full' means it covered the entire cost, not just part of it.
quests.textToSpeak: She received a full scholarship to study engineering abroad.
quests.textWithBlanks: She received a full ___ to study engineering abroad.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: The past form of 'reschedule' — to arrange a new time for something already planned.
quests.explanation: Rescheduled means moved to a new time, similar to 'postponed' but emphasising that a new date was actually set. 'Unexpected building repairs' explains the reason clearly.
quests.textToSpeak: The conference was rescheduled due to unexpected building repairs.
quests.textWithBlanks: The conference was ___ due to unexpected building repairs.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: An experienced person who guides and advises someone less experienced.
quests.explanation: A mentor offers guidance based on their own experience. This relationship is widely recognised as valuable, especially at the start of a career.
quests.textToSpeak: Having a good mentor early in your career can make a huge difference.
quests.textWithBlanks: Having a good ___ early in your career can make a huge difference.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: The past form of 'acquire' — for one company to buy and take control of another.
quests.explanation: Acquired means bought and taken over, a word commonly used about companies. 'Much larger corporation' shows a typical, unequal business acquisition.
quests.textToSpeak: The small tech company was acquired by a much larger corporation last year.
quests.textWithBlanks: The small tech company was ___ by a much larger corporation last year.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Widely admired and respected, often because of high status or achievement.
quests.explanation: Prestigious describes something associated with great respect and status. Awards, universities, and jobs are often described this way.
quests.textToSpeak: Winning such a prestigious award changed the course of her career.
quests.textWithBlanks: Winning such a ___ award changed the course of her career.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Strong public disagreement or argument about a subject, often dividing opinion.
quests.explanation: Controversy describes a topic that causes strong, divided public opinion. 'Sparked' is the verb almost always used when something suddenly causes this kind of debate.
quests.textToSpeak: The new policy sparked considerable controversy among local residents.
quests.textWithBlanks: The new policy sparked considerable ___ among local residents.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: No longer needed for a job, typically because of company cutbacks or closure.
quests.explanation: Redundant describes losing a job because it's no longer needed, not because of poor performance. 'The factory closed' explains the reason clearly and without blame.
quests.textToSpeak: Two hundred workers were made redundant when the factory closed.
quests.textWithBlanks: Two hundred workers were made ___ when the factory closed.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: The past form of 'anticipate' — to look forward to something expected to happen.
quests.explanation: Anticipated means eagerly expected or awaited. 'Almost two years' shows just how long fans had been looking forward to it.
quests.textToSpeak: The film's release was anticipated for almost two years.
quests.textWithBlanks: The film's release was ___ for almost two years.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: A written text, especially a book, before it has been printed.
quests.explanation: A manuscript is an author's completed text before publication. 'Before finding a publisher' shows this stage happens well before a book ever reaches shops.
quests.textToSpeak: She spent five years writing the manuscript before finding a publisher.
quests.textWithBlanks: She spent five years writing the ___ before finding a publisher.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: The past form of 'jeopardise' — to put something at serious risk of harm or failure.
quests.explanation: Jeopardised means put something valuable at serious risk. 'One careless mistake' shows how little it can take to threaten a whole agreement.
quests.textToSpeak: One careless mistake nearly jeopardised the entire deal.
quests.textWithBlanks: One careless mistake nearly ___ the entire deal.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Qualified or allowed to do or receive something because you meet the requirements.
quests.explanation: Eligible describes meeting the specific conditions needed for something. 'Two years' service' is the precise requirement mentioned here.
quests.textToSpeak: Only employees with two years' service are eligible for the bonus.
quests.textWithBlanks: Only employees with two years' service are ___ for the bonus.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: A formal statement, especially one given as evidence in a court of law.
quests.explanation: Testimony is evidence given, often spoken, particularly in legal settings. 'Crucial to the final verdict' shows just how important her statement turned out to be.
quests.textToSpeak: Her testimony in court proved crucial to the final verdict.
quests.textWithBlanks: Her ___ in court proved crucial to the final verdict.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: The past form of 'liaise' — to communicate and cooperate closely with another person or group.
quests.explanation: Liaised means worked closely with another team through regular communication. This word is common in professional and workplace English.
quests.textToSpeak: She liaised closely with the design team throughout the project.
quests.textWithBlanks: She ___ closely with the design team throughout the project.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: A serious attempt to achieve something difficult.
quests.explanation: Endeavour describes a determined attempt at something challenging, often admirable. 'Biggest... of his life' shows just how significant this attempt was to him.
quests.textToSpeak: Starting a business from nothing was the biggest endeavour of his life.
quests.textWithBlanks: Starting a business from nothing was the biggest ___ of his life.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Successful, respected, and admired, especially because of achievements in a career.
quests.explanation: Distinguished describes someone whose career achievements have earned wide respect. This word appears often when formally introducing respected guests or speakers.
quests.textToSpeak: A distinguished professor gave the opening lecture at the conference.
quests.textWithBlanks: A ___ professor gave the opening lecture at the conference.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: The past form of 'forfeit' — to lose something automatically because of breaking a rule or missing a deadline.
quests.explanation: Forfeited means automatically lost something due to a rule violation. Arriving late enough to lose a match by default is a strict but real consequence.
quests.textToSpeak: The team forfeited the match after arriving twenty minutes late.
quests.textWithBlanks: The team ___ the match after arriving twenty minutes late.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Very small in amount, barely enough to be sufficient.
quests.explanation: Meagre describes an amount that is uncomfortably small. 'First year abroad' suggests they were still adjusting to new financial pressures.
quests.textToSpeak: They survived on a meagre budget during their first year abroad.
quests.textWithBlanks: They survived on a ___ budget during their first year abroad.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Documents or qualifications that prove a person's identity, ability, or authority.
quests.explanation: Credentials are official proof of identity or qualification. 'Restricted area' explains why this level of verification was necessary.
quests.textToSpeak: He was asked to show his credentials before entering the restricted area.
quests.textWithBlanks: He was asked to show his ___ before entering the restricted area.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: The past form of 'revoke' — to officially cancel a right, licence, or agreement.
quests.explanation: Revoked means officially cancelled or taken away, often as a penalty. 'Third offence' shows this was a consequence of repeated rule-breaking.
quests.textToSpeak: His driving licence was revoked after the third offence.
quests.textWithBlanks: His driving licence was ___ after the third offence.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: The past form of 'advocate' — to publicly support a particular cause or policy.
quests.explanation: Advocated means publicly argued in support of something. 'After the incident' shows the specific event that prompted this stance.
quests.textToSpeak: The senator advocated for stricter safety laws after the incident.
quests.textWithBlanks: The senator ___ for stricter safety laws after the incident.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Not favouring one side over another; fair and unbiased.
quests.explanation: Impartial describes complete fairness, without favouring either side. This is one of the most essential qualities expected of a judge.
quests.textToSpeak: A judge must remain completely impartial throughout the trial.
quests.textWithBlanks: A judge must remain completely ___ throughout the trial.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: A situation in which something harmful spreads quickly and affects a great many people.
quests.explanation: Epidemic originally described the fast spread of disease but is now often used for other fast-spreading problems too. This wider modern usage is very common in the media.
quests.textToSpeak: Officials described the rise in fake news as an epidemic of misinformation.
quests.textWithBlanks: Officials described the rise in fake news as an ___ of misinformation.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: With everyone in complete agreement; with no one disagreeing.
quests.explanation: Unanimously describes total agreement, without a single dissenting vote. This shows unusually strong, shared support for the board's decision.
quests.textToSpeak: The board voted unanimously to approve the merger.
quests.textWithBlanks: The board voted ___ to approve the merger.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: People or groups with a genuine interest in, or who are affected by, a decision.
quests.explanation: Stakeholders are people or organisations affected by or invested in a decision. Involving them 'before the vote' shows a fair, transparent process.
quests.textToSpeak: The proposal was presented to all major stakeholders before the vote.
quests.textWithBlanks: The proposal was presented to all major ___ before the vote.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Never stopping or weakening, despite difficulty or opposition.
quests.explanation: Relentless describes unstoppable persistence despite obstacles. 'Years of setbacks' shows exactly what this determination had to overcome.
quests.textToSpeak: Her relentless determination eventually paid off after years of setbacks.
quests.textWithBlanks: Her ___ determination eventually paid off after years of setbacks.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: The past form of 'denounce' — to strongly and publicly criticise something as wrong.
quests.explanation: Denounced means publicly and strongly condemned something. This word is common in formal statements from governments and officials.
quests.textToSpeak: World leaders denounced the attack as a violation of international law.
quests.textWithBlanks: World leaders ___ the attack as a violation of international law.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: The often unpleasant effects or results of an action, felt some time later.
quests.explanation: Repercussions are consequences that appear after the fact, often unwanted. 'Long-term' emphasises that these effects weren't immediately obvious.
quests.textToSpeak: Nobody had considered the long-term repercussions of the decision.
quests.textWithBlanks: Nobody had considered the long-term ___ of the decision.
